analysis: Evidence shows two policy-compliant successes (task 66: correctly refused same-product-type change and guided to cancellation; task 92: handled multi-order returns with confirmation) and one failure (task 29: complex cross-order 'swap delivered item for pending-order item' scenario). The successes are already adequately covered by the native policy (authentication, status checks, same-product-type restriction, explicit confirmation before updates, gathering all items before each call). The failure's root cause is ambiguous: plausible causes include making three tool calls in a single turn versus an unsanctioned modification of the pending order that altered its contents, and we cannot determine which (if either) the evaluator penalized. A similarly parallel multi-call turn in task 92 succeeded, making the multi-call explanation contradictory. Without knowing the hidden reference behavior, encoding guidance from this one-off complex failure risks overfitting and regressions. No reusable capability gap is clearly demonstrated beyond what the policy already specifies, so no skill change is warranted.
